1 01. 1.
Since all the three cases are arising out of one F.I.R., all are heard together and disposed of by this // 2 // common order.

2. Heard.
3.

At the instance of the opposite party no.2, the F.I.R., i.e., Angul P.S. Case No.447 of 2021 came to be registered against the petitioners under Sections 376/506/323/34 of the IPC pending in the Court of learned J.M.F.C., Banarpal.

3. The allegation as per the F.I.R. is that one Rajib Agarwal developed friendship with respondent no 2 and taking advantage of her loneliess, committed rape on her against her will, took photos and videos of her and started blackmailing her.

However, keeping in view the prestige of her family, she remained silent but few days after on 25.08.2021, the son of Rajib Agarwal, namely, Rakesh Agarwal came to her house and forcibly committed rape on her and threatened her of dire consequences.
Hence, the F.I.R. was lodged.

4. After investigation, charge sheet has been submitted on 30.09.2021 against the petitioners for commission alleged offences under Sections 4 & 5 of the Immoral Traffic Act and subsequently, on 22.10.2021, the learned Magistrate has taken cognizance for the same offences.
4. When the matter stood thus, the parties have settled their dispute.

The opposite party no.2 has filed an affidavit dated 14.02.2023 inter alia stating as under:
"3. That, prior to registration my case the accused Abhishek Agrawal lodged a FIR //
3 // against me as well as my husband and same has been registered as Angul P.S.
Case No.446 of 2021 which corresponding to G.R. Case No.901 of 2021 pending in the court of learned J.M.F.C., Angul.
4. That, due to some misunderstanding I had lodged FIR against abovenamed accused persons now a compromise has been taken place between us in presence of our family members and relatives.
In view of compromise we both have deiced to withdraw the case filed by us against each other.
5. That, in view of the compromise, I do not want to proceed with the case further and if the proceeding will be quashed by the Hon'ble Court, then I have no objection."
5. The petitioners and opposite party no.2 are present in the Court today along with their respective counsel and identified by them.
They have also filed their self attested copies of the Aadhaar Cards to establish their identity, which are taken on record.
6. Apparently, the petitioner in CRLMC No.1846 of 2022 has filed a counter case against the opposite party no.2 being Angul P.S. Case No.446 of 2021.
The parties have settled their dispute.
In order to quash the cross FIR CRLMC No.351 of 2023 has been filed,which is listed today.

2 7. Mr. Ragada, learned counsel for the State submits that although the F.I.R. has been filed by the parties against each other and due to misunderstanding in the business being carried out by them and they have already settled their dispute, there is no legal // 4 // impediment to quash the F.I.R.
8.

Regard being had to the aforementioned facts and the opposite party no.2 is not willing to proceed against the petitioners, I am of the considered view that the case of the present petitioner is squarely covered by the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and another reported in 2012 (10) SCC 303 and B.S. Joshi & others vs. State of Haryana &
another reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675

In the aforementioned circumstances subjecting the petitioners to trial in the present case would be a futile excise.

9. Taking into consideration the aforementioned judgments, facts of the case and submission made at bar, Angul P.S. Case No.447 of 2021 corresponding to G.R. Case No.902 of 2021 pending in the Court of learned J.M.F.C., Banarpal and the consequential proceedings arising therefrom qua the petitioners are quashed.
10. The CRLMC is accordingly disposed of.
